doc.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022

title: The Willow Weep for Me, Satisfaction and Beer Barrel Polka medley
summary: Ries explains how the medley arose, with Al's accordion and his memory of playing polkas in his dad's band.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well I’m pretty sure you made musical history last night because I’m going to guess that there’s never been a medley of “Willow Weep for Me” into “I Can’t Get No Satisfaction” into the “Beer Barrel Polka.” So congratulations.

Wow. And I did not plan that in any way it just — oh my God well I realized ‘cause we were going to go until ten o’clock. And I looked at my watch and it was like oh so maybe we were in “Willow Weep for Me” at like ten to ten because I didn’t want to go too much past that or whatever, and I thought well I’ll play “Satisfaction” ‘cause if there are Stones fans there they want to do that, so we went into that and I saw Al in the front again and the accordion was still out and I thought well how do we get Al up again. And then he comes up and I didn’t think about the “Beer Barrel Polka” but he was playing. And Ron was saying, “Just play on C.” And I thought well but you know he’s trying to think how can I play and I thought you know what? Everyone knows this polka. Certainly Al would

know it, and I know Ron knows it and I used to play polkas in my dad’s band ‘cause that’s one thing, you have to play rock, you have to play Irving Berlin, and you’ve got to play a polka because somebody might want to dance to that. So I just thought well if I play that Al’s going to be able to jump in, which he did. So it was like — again how do you make it work with all — here you have one of the Polka Kings there, you’ve got to have him play a polka.
I love the end. Not everybody would be able to do that, like well say I’m in this key the melody, and then you do that boom in your head like in an instant.

Well I was trying to think of another polka that would be even more un — sort of like obscure that like Al would be like wow you know that? But in my head I was like also it’s getting late and at ten o’clock I thought okay surely everybody in the room would know that and that’s why when Ron did that then everyone could join and sing. So then it became like the whole room could be part of it.
